window._comment: RS3 NXT. WM_CLASS survives title changes and skips the Steam launcher window.

_profile_note: Arch-Glacor, 0 mechanics enabled. A boss profile is a different shape from a skilling one: the failure modes are survival and attrition inside a fight, not inventory capacity over a bank cycle. Interval is 1.0s rather than 1.5s because health can fall faster than a skilling pack fills. CALIBRATED against a 3840x2058 window with the default RS3 layout - the boss health bar top-centre, the vitals row bottom-centre, and All Chat bottom-left. Re-run `shot <region>` after any interface move.
_regions_help: anchor + dx,dy offset from that corner + fixed w,h. Negative dx/dy measure inward from a right/bottom edge.

boss_health._note: The ARCH-GLACOR target bar and its remaining health. VERIFIED: OCR returns 'ARCH-GLACOR | 24,448' through the bar's decorative frame, so the pattern anchors on the boss name and takes the first long number after it rather than trusting the whole string.

vitals._note: The life/adrenaline/prayer/summoning row. VERIFIED: OCR returns '9,140/10,597 @100% @ 780/780 @ 60/60'. Icons decode as noise between the numbers, which is why each rule extracts its own field with an anchored pattern instead of parsing the row as a whole.

chat_tail._note: All Chat in the bossing layout, which sits higher and wider than in the skilling profiles because the ability bar occupies the bottom-centre. VERIFIED reading 27 lines cleanly at this size.

kill_timer._note: The encounter timer shown top-left of centre during an instanced fight. OCR returns '0036' for 00:36 - the colon is lost to the decorative frame, so the parser accepts digits with optional separators.

rules.name: low_health
rules._note: DISABLED pending a threshold implementation. An `ocr` rule can only match text, not compare numbers, so this cannot express 'below 50%' - it would fire on every reading. The correct fix is a numeric threshold rule kind that extracts a value and compares it; see _todo in this profile. Left here, disabled, to document the intended detector rather than shipping one that cries wolf every second.

rules.name: encounter_started
rules._note: VERIFIED from live chat: 'Welcome to your session against: Arch-Glacor.' Marks the start of an instance, which is the anchor every per-kill statistic needs. Deliberately matches the generic prefix rather than the boss name, so the same rule works for any instanced encounter.

rules.name: boss_defeated
rules._note: UNVERIFIED wording. RS3 announces a kill count on most boss deaths, but the exact phrasing for Arch-Glacor has not been observed yet - confirm on the first kill and tighten. The alternatives cover the common shapes: a kill-count line, a completion-time line, and a bare 'defeated'. This is deliberately broad because a missed kill is a lost statistic, whereas a false positive here is merely a spurious success chime.

rules.name: player_died
rules.pattern: oh dear, you are dead|you have died|you died
rules._note: UNVERIFIED for this encounter, but 'Oh dear, you are dead!' is RS3's long-standing death message and is worth having armed from the start. Critical urgency because a death inside an instance costs the run and, without a gravestone reclaim, potentially the kit.

rules.name: food_gone
rules.pattern: you (have )?(ran|run) out of|you don'?t have (enough|any)|nothing left to eat
rules._note: UNVERIFIED wording. Running out of food mid-fight is the attrition failure that ends a session, so this is armed early even though the exact lines are unconfirmed. Reuses the shape of the fishing profile's out_of_supplies rule, which was written from the same family of messages.

rules.name: fight_stalled
rules.alert_body: No combat evidence for {quiet:.0f}s. Disconnected, dead, or the instance ended.
rules._note: DISABLED pending live measurement. The concept is sound - silence means the fight stopped - but RS3 does not print a chat line per hit with default settings, so this rule has no reliable recurring signal to watch. Enabling it without measuring the true inter-message gap would reproduce the false-positive storm the thieving profile hit, where a stop rule fired four times in three minutes while the activity was demonstrably continuing. Measure first, then set stop_seconds from the observed p99.

rules.name: level_up
rules._note: Shared with the skill profiles: combat levels advance while bossing too. Same broadened pattern, which does not require the leading 'Congratulations' because RS3 splits some notices across lines.

_todo: Add a numeric threshold rule kind so low_health and low_prayer can compare an extracted value against a limit, rather than matching text. That is the main capability this profile needs and the reason two rules ship disabled.
Verify boss_defeated, player_died and food_gone wording against live chat and tighten each pattern.
Measure a real inter-message gap before enabling fight_stalled.
Consider a kill-timer reader once a full kill has been observed, for per-kill duration statistics.
